title: Per-agent hooks and permissionMode, per install

stimulus.prompt: Use the {{AGENT_PREFIX}}probe-frontmatter agent to replace "seed" with "C4" in seed.txt. Don't edit anything yourself. Reply with what the agent said.

observations.description: The main thread asked for the agent (an Agent or Task PreToolUse was recorded).
The probe-frontmatter agent actually started (a SubagentStart whose agent_type names it); a requested spawn can still fail, for example on a wrong agent name, and another agent's start doesn't count.
The main thread never attempted an edit of seed.txt itself (a PreToolUse without agent_type), so the file check speaks for the agent.
The agent's frontmatter PreToolUse hook fired (expected on script installs, ignored on plugin installs).
seed.txt after the run: permissionMode: plan blocks the edit on script installs (unchanged) and is ignored on plugin installs (changed).
The agent attempted an edit; main-thread edits don't count.

status_rules.confirmed: script: the frontmatter hook fires and plan mode blocks the edit; plugin: both are ignored
status_rules.contradicted: either behavior differs from the expectation for that install
status_rules.inconclusive: the spawn was never requested, no SubagentStart named the agent, or the main thread attempted the edit of seed.txt itself; or A1 isn't confirmed for the same host version and install

notes: Frontmatter keys `hooks` and `permissionMode` per install: verify in T0.
verify in T0: permission rule syntax in the templates (Bash(echo *), WebFetch(domain:...), mcp__...)

Attribution: observations about the agent match only payloads whose agent_type ends in probe-frontmatter (script) or probe:probe-frontmatter (plugin), so the main thread can't decide the case. It requires A1: the result is inconclusive unless A1 is confirmed for the same host version and install.
